questions.question:
Solution: Configure the call queue to use a team and channel.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Mapping a Teams call queue to a team and channel provides the most versatile queue experience. Shared voicemail forwarded by a call queue connected to a Microsoft 365 Group channel is available in that channel’s **Calls** section, and queue call history can be shared with agents when shared call history is enabled. Using the team’s group membership minimizes separate administrative access configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Routing calls with Auto attendants and Call queues for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/plan-your-call-routing-flow) · [Manage Shared Voicemail for Auto Attendants and Call Queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-shared-voicemail)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure group call pickup for the call queue.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Group call pickup shares incoming calls for an individual user with colleagues; it does not provide call-queue history or shared voicemail. Microsoft Teams shared call history for call queues enables agents to view queue activity and shared voicemails, including voicemail-related records, when configured for the call queue.\
\
**Learn more:** [Call sharing and group call pickup - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup) · [Setup - Shared Call History for Call Queue - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-call-queue-shared-history)

questions.question:
Solution: Redirect calls from the call queue to a shared voicemail box.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A shared voicemail destination provides group access to voicemail messages and transcriptions, but it does not by itself provide call queue history. Queue agents can view shared call history only when a shared call-history template is configured for the call queue; this exposes queue call records and shared voicemails to the permitted agents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Setup - Shared Call History for Call Queue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-call-queue-shared-history) · [Manage Shared Voicemail for Auto Attendants and Call Queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-shared-voicemail)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure the call queue’s routing method as **Attendant routing**.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Attendant routing is a call-distribution setting and does not provide agents with shared call-queue history or configure shared transcribed voicemail. Shared call history must be enabled through a shared call-history template, and shared voicemail must be configured as a call-queue exception destination.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up call queues in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-call-queue) · [Shared call history for Call Queue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-call-queue-shared-history)

questions.explanation:
A Direct Routing deployment connects Teams Phone to existing PSTN and PBX infrastructure through a certified Session Border Controller (SBC). An E1/T1 PRI is a physical digital trunk, so retaining that service requires an SBC with a physical PRI interface to terminate and route the trunk. An ATA supports analog telephony rather than PRI, and virtual or Azure-hosted SBCs cannot directly terminate the on-premises PRI circuit.

**Learn more:** [Configure Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-configure) · [Microsoft Teams call flows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/microsoft-teams-online-call-flows)

Your company has a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment that uses Direct Routing and one carrier.  
  
You deploy a new Session Border Controller (SBC), which appears healthy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.  
  
You make a test call through the new SBC, and the call is successful.  
  
When you try to transfer the call, the transfer fails. Part of the SIP ladder is displayed in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784112280257-a461dgxc.png)  
  
What could be causing the issue?

options.text: NOTIFY is enabled in the SIP options of the SBC.
The carrier rejects the format of the forwarded FROM number.
The SSL certificate of the SBC is incorrect.
The Refer on the SBC is misconfigured.

questions.explanation:
For a Direct Routing call transfer in which the SBC receives a SIP REFER, the SBC must process the REFER and initiate a new INVITE back to the Microsoft SIP proxy using the transfer information. Accepting the REFER and sending NOTIFY messages without correctly performing that transfer flow causes the transfer to fail; this indicates that REFER handling on the SBC is misconfigured.

**Learn more:** [Direct Routing – SIP protocol](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-protocols-sip) · [Issues that affect call transfers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/phone-system/direct-routing/issues-with-call-transfers)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
You use Direct Routing with a Survivable Branch Appliance (SBA) at a site.  
  
The site has an extended internet outage.  
  
Which three PSTN calling scenarios can occur during the outage? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: hold and resume of PSTN calls

questions.explanation:
During an internet outage, Teams clients operating through a local Survivable Branch Appliance can make PSTN calls, receive PSTN calls, and place PSTN calls on hold and resume them. Dynamic emergency calling depends on location information services and is not available in SBA offline mode; emergency calls can still be placed, but location information is not shared. Microsoft documents blind transfer specifically rather than unrestricted PSTN call transfer.

**Learn more:** [Direct Routing SBA - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-survivable-branch-appliance)

What must the SBC support to enable media bypass?
questions.explanation:
Teams Direct Routing media bypass uses ICE between the Teams client and the SBC. The SBC must support the ICE Lite protocol so it can participate in ICE connectivity checks and establish the direct media path.\
\
**Learn more:** [Direct Routing support for media bypass](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-protocols-media) · [Plan for media bypass with Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-plan-media-bypass)

What should you do within the Microsoft Team admin center?

Create a configuration profile for IP phones.
Register the handsets by using remote provisioning.

Teams webinars provide presenter bios, attendee registration, and registration-management capabilities. You plan to deploy Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that lets users make and receive calls using one phone number shared by a company-provided smartphone, a desk phone, and Teams. The solution must minimize costs and the number of phone numbers purchased from an operator.  
  
What should be included in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Teams Phone Mobile makes a user’s SIM-enabled, company-owned mobile number also their Teams number. Calls to that number ring the smartphone and active Teams clients, and the number can be used on Teams endpoints such as desk phones. Using one operator-provided number for these endpoints minimizes the number of purchased phone numbers.\
\

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You need to ensure that a user named [email protected] can use Direct Routing to call international phone numbers.  
  
Which type of policy should you use?
questions.explanation:
A voice routing policy is assigned to Direct Routing users and contains PSTN usages that link to voice routes. Configure the applicable PSTN usage and voice route for the international number pattern, then assign the voice routing policy to the user.\
\

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You need to ensure that users can enter their emergency address in the Teams client.  
  
Which setting should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Enabling **External location lookup mode** in a Teams emergency calling policy allows users to add, edit, or confirm their emergency address from the Teams Calls client, including for remote locations.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment containing the following accounts:  
  
- User1  
- User2  
- CallQueue1

You plan to implement Shared Calling.  
  
To which accounts should you assign a dedicated phone number?
questions.explanation:
Shared Calling uses the phone number of a resource account associated with an Auto attendant for inbound and outbound PSTN calls, so individual users do not require dedicated phone numbers. The Auto attendant can route calls to a call queue, which does not need its own dedicated number for this deployment.

questions.question:
You have a Teams Phone deployment.  
  
A Survivable Branch Appliance (SBA) with local PSTN connectivity is deployed at a remote site.  
  
Which two features need internet connectivity to function? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
An SBA maintains local PSTN calling during an internet outage, including media bypass and basic local call handling. SBA mode does not support dynamic emergency-calling capabilities such as sharing E911 location information or Emergency Call Routing Policies. The cloud-managed call-forwarding feature requires connectivity for its full Teams service behavior.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a newly deployed Teams Phone environment.  
  
Users must be able to dial a five-digit phone number to reach other users in the same office.  
  
You determine that the five-digit number does **not** translate to an E.164 number.  
  
What should you review to troubleshoot this issue?
questions.explanation:
Teams dial plans use normalization rules to translate abbreviated internal dial strings, such as five-digit extensions, into standardized numbers, typically in E.164 format, before routing. Review the applicable dial plan and its normalization rules when that translation does not occur.

**Learn more:** [Normalization rules for Microsoft Teams dial plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phone-normalization-rules) · [Planning Teams dial plans for Teams Phone](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/dial-plans-routing-overview)

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, create a configuration profile for Teams displays.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, create a configuration profile for Teams Phone.

questions.explanation:
Hotline (also called PLAR) is enabled in the Microsoft Teams admin center from a configuration profile assigned to Teams phones. The profile’s Call settings include the **Enable hotline** option, which can then be applied to the target devices.\

What should you do?

options.text: The failover timer is set to 0 seconds.

The firewall blocks traffic on port 5067.

questions.explanation:
For Direct Routing, the SBC’s configured SIP signaling port is its TLS listening port. Microsoft’s SIP proxy must be able to reach that port on the SBC. Blocking traffic on port 5067 prevents the TLS/SIP connection from being established, leaving TLS connectivity inactive and preventing calls.

**Learn more:** [Connect your Session Border Controller (SBC) to Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-connect-the-sbc) · [Plan Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-plan)

options.text: Assign the Teams Premium license to all users.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You have a site named Site1 that includes a Session Border Controller (SBC) named SBC2. SBC2 uses Direct Routing and does **not** have local internet connectivity.  
  
Site1 has an MPLS connection to a datacenter hosting another SBC named SBC1. SBC1 uses Direct Routing.  
  
You need to provide Enterprise Voice to Site1 users by configuring SBC2 to use SBC1.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A proxy SBC configuration makes the centrally connected SBC act as the intermediary for a downstream SBC. This allows SBC2 to use SBC1 for its Direct Routing path when SBC2 lacks its own local internet connectivity. Microsoft documents the `ProxySBC` setting for assigning a proxy SBC to a Direct Routing SBC.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment that includes two users, User1 and User2.  
  
User1 will be away on leave for two weeks.  
  
You need to redirect every call to User1's phone number to User2's phone number. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you modify for User1?

options.text: the call delay and order settings

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams Phone call delegation allows a delegate to receive and manage calls on behalf of another user. Configuring User2 as User1’s delegate provides the appropriate call-handling relationship for temporarily directing User1’s incoming calls to User2. Call-group delay/order settings, voicemail transfer targets, and phone-number type do not establish this call routing.

**Learn more:** [Configure call forwarding and delegation settings - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/shared-line-appearance)

You are deploying Microsoft Teams Rooms. The first time you try to sign in to a Teams Rooms, you receive an error message that the device cannot sign in to Teams. You verify that Modern authentication is enabled in Teams Rooms.

options.text: Teams Rooms must be domain-joined first
MFA is unsupported in Teams Rooms
The Microsoft Authenticator app is not configured for the Teams Rooms account

questions.explanation:

You plan to deploy Teams Rooms by using a `SkypeSettings.xml` file.  
  
Which two actions can you perform in the file? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Allow remote control from personal devices.

questions.explanation:
The `AllowRoomRemoteEnabled` XML element allows room-remote connections from personal devices, and `AutoAcceptProximateMeetingInvitations` automatically accepts proximity-based meeting invitations. Both are Teams Rooms settings configurable through `SkypeSettings.xml`.\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You have a legacy PBX audio-conferencing solution that includes a dial-in toll number.  
  
You need to migrate the dial-in toll number to Teams meetings.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, assign Teams Audio Conferencing add-on licenses to the users.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, assign Teams Phone Standard add-on licenses to the users.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Phone numbers, select Numbers, and then select Port
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Phone numbers, select Numbers, and then select Add

questions.explanation:
An existing toll number used for audio conferencing must be transferred to Microsoft by creating a port order. Teams supports porting existing service numbers for Audio Conferencing conference bridges; the Teams admin center’s **Phone numbers** area is used to initiate that port request. Microsoft 365 E5 already includes Audio Conferencing, so an Audio Conferencing add-on is not the prerequisite.

**Learn more:** [What's a port order? - Planning to transfer telephone numbers to Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/microsoftteams/phone-number-calling-plans/port-order-overview) · [Set up Audio Conferencing for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-audio-conferencing-in-teams?azure-portal=true)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named contoso.com.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy Microsoft Teams Rooms shared-room video conferencing.  
  
You deploy 50 Teams Rooms on Windows devices and join every device to contoso.com.  
  
You need to enable Direct Guest Join on all 50 devices. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Guest access settings.
Deploy a SkypeSettings.xml file to each device by using Group Policy.

questions.explanation:
Direct Guest Join for Teams Rooms on Windows is enabled through device settings in `SkypeSettings.xml`, such as the settings for Cisco Webex, Zoom, and Google Meet. A Group Policy can copy that common configuration file to all domain-joined devices, providing centralized deployment with minimal administrative effort.

**Learn more:** [Manage a Microsoft Teams Rooms console settings remotely with an XML configuration file](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/xml-config-file) · [Third-party meetings on Teams Rooms](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/third-party-join)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment with 10 offices. Each office has a Session Border Controller (SBC).  
  
A user reports that she can place internal calls by using the dial pad, but she cannot use the dial pad to place external calls.  
  
What could be causing the issue?

options.text: The user is missing a validated emergency address
The user has the incorrect voice routing policy applied
Enterprise Voice is disabled for the user
The user has the incorrect Teams app setup policy applied

questions.explanation:
For Teams Direct Routing, a voice routing policy assigns PSTN usages to users. Those usages select voice routes and the associated SBCs for external PSTN calls. If the user has an incorrect voice routing policy, no matching external route may be available even though internal Teams calls still work.

**Learn more:** [Manage call routing policies for Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-voice-routing-policies) · [Configure call routing for Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-voice-routing)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
You have offices in the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil, India, and China.  
  
You will use Direct Routing at all locations.  
  
You need to create a network topology for roaming bandwidth policies.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Implement dynamic emergency calling with Presence Information Data Format Location Object (PIDF-LO).
Add the Teams client public IP addresses to the Trusted IPs list.
Set Preferred country or region for media traffic for the Session Border Controller (SBC).
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, assign a usage location.

questions.explanation:
Teams network roaming policies are assigned to network sites, so network sites are required for location-based roaming bandwidth settings. For Direct Routing, an SBC can be configured with a preferred country or region for media traffic by using its media relay routing location override, which helps select the appropriate media relay region for the SBC.

**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [Direct Routing media path country and region codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-country-codes)

options.text: The Forward P-Asserted Identify (PAI) header is disabled.
The Digicert root certificate is missing on the SBC.
Location-Based Routing is enabled for the SBC.

questions.explanation:
Direct Routing relies on mutual TLS between the SBC and the Teams SIP proxy. Microsoft’s Direct Routing troubleshooting guidance identifies an SBC not trusting the SIP proxy certificate as a TLS connection issue.

A Direct Routing SBC must trust the certificate chain used by the Teams SIP proxy. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment that uses Direct Routing. The deployment includes these configurations:

- Teams client external IP subnet: 203.0.113.0/24  
- Teams client internal IP subnet: 192.168.0.0/24  
  
You need to configure the network topology to support emergency-call routing.  
  
Which network range should be added to the trusted IP addresses?
questions.explanation:
Teams trusted IP addresses are the organization’s external public IP ranges used to determine whether a Teams client endpoint is inside the corporate network. Adding the Teams client external subnet enables Teams to match the client’s public source address and use the network topology for emergency calling. Internal client ranges are configured as network subnets, while an SBC public address and Microsoft service ranges are not client external trusted IP ranges.

questions.explanation:
Call delegation, also known as shared line appearance, lets a delegate make and receive calls on behalf of a delegator. A call queue can be assigned a resource-account phone number for inbound calls, and its representatives can make outbound calls on behalf of that queue. These features therefore support shared use of one number for both inbound and outbound calling.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a branch office named Branch1 that includes a Survivable Branch Appliance (SBA) in Microsoft Teams.  
  
You have deployed Teams Phone.  
  
A limited number of Branch1 users report that they cannot make Teams calls when the office internet connection fails.  
  
You need to ensure that every user in Branch1 can make calls during an internet outage.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign an SBA policy to the users in Branch1.
Reregister the SBA with Azure AD.
Reconfigure the PSTN trunk settings for the SBA.
Assign a dial-out policy to the users in Branch1.

questions.explanation:
During an internet outage, a Teams client can switch to SBA mode and make or receive PSTN calls only when the user is assigned the branch survivability policy that identifies the available SBA. Assigning the SBA policy to all Branch1 users supplies that required policy association.

**Learn more:** [Direct Routing SBA - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-survivable-branch-appliance)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an office in Atlanta. The company has a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment that includes a toll-free phone number.  
  
You find that the Atlanta office has significantly high toll-free dial-in usage for meetings. You need to disable the toll-free number for meetings organized by users in the Atlanta office.  
  
Which type of policy should you configure in the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation:
An Audio Conferencing policy controls whether toll-free numbers are included in meeting invitations created by assigned users. Assigning a policy with toll-free dial-in disabled to the Atlanta meeting organizers prevents participants from using the organization’s toll-free number for their meetings.

**Learn more:** [Disabling toll-free numbers for specific Teams users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/disabling-toll-free-numbers-for-specific-teams-users) · [Teams settings and policies reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/settings-policies-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment and a Survivable Branch Appliance (SBA) at a site.  
  
You add a new Teams user.  
  
You need to ensure that the user at the site can make and receive PSTN calls if an internet outage occurs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the user as a member of a call queue.
Modify the online voice routing policy.

questions.explanation:
An SBA policy must be assigned to the user so the user is associated with the Survivable Branch Appliance and can continue placing and receiving PSTN calls during a service or internet outage. `Grant-CsTeamsSurvivableBranchAppliancePolicy` assigns that policy to an individual user.

You have a Microsoft Teams deployment.  
  
A user named User1 intends to host a live event.  
  
You create a new meeting policy and configure **Screen sharing mode** as **Entire screen**.  
  
You need to finish configuring the meeting policy so that User1 can host the live event.  
  
Which two settings should you turn **On**? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Broadcast production with NDI and SDI hardware

questions.explanation:
A Teams live-event organizer needs permission to schedule private meetings and must have video conferencing enabled, in addition to the already enabled entire-screen sharing. The private-meeting scheduling setting permits scheduling, while Video Conferencing permits video in meetings hosted by the user. NDI/SDI broadcast production is only needed for an external broadcast-hardware workflow.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams deployment.  
  
You plan to deploy Teams Rooms devices.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that supports the following features:

Which Teams Rooms configuration should you recommend?

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Teams Phone deployment that uses Direct Routing with a single Session Border Controller (SBC).  
  
Users report that outbound PSTN calls fail, while inbound PSTN calls succeed.  
  
After reviewing the SBC logs, you find that Microsoft responds to SIP OPTIONS requests but does **not** send SIP OPTIONS requests.  
  
What is causing the issue?

options.text: The online PSTN gateway is disabled.
An external DNS entry is missing from the FQDN of the SBC.
The phone numbers of the users are defined by running the New-csTeamsUnassignedNumberTreatment cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
For Direct Routing, after Microsoft receives OPTIONS from an SBC, it sends outbound SIP OPTIONS to the SBC FQDN specified in the SBC's Contact header. That FQDN must resolve publicly to the correct SBC address. A missing external DNS entry prevents Microsoft from initiating signaling to the SBC, which blocks outbound PSTN calls even though the SBC can initiate signaling to Microsoft for inbound calls.

**Learn more:** [Connect your Session Border Controller (SBC) to Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-connect-the-sbc) · [SBC connectivity issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/phone-system/direct-routing/sip-options-tls-certificate-issues)

You deploy Microsoft Teams Rooms.  
  
During a meeting, participants report that when they use the Front Row meeting layout, the video size is too small.  
  
You need to increase the video size in the Front Row meeting layout.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams Rooms uses the `FrontRowVideoSize` element in its XML configuration file to control how much space Front Row allocates to remote-participant video versus shared content. Valid values include `small`, `medium`, and `large`; using `large` increases the video size.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage a Microsoft Teams Rooms console settings remotely with an XML configuration file](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/xml-config-file)

Your Microsoft 365 subscription uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You have a room named Room1 that contains 10 desks.  
  
You need to configure Room1 as a bookable desk pool.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a resource account for Room1.
Purchase a Teams Rooms Basic license.
Create a resource account for the desk pool.

questions.explanation:
A bookable desk pool is represented by an Exchange workspace resource account. Its capacity is configured to the number of available seats, allowing multiple users to reserve the pool until its capacity is exhausted. The desk-pool resource account must be created before its booking settings can be configured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Setting up Bookable Desks in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/bookable-desks)

You need to configure a content camera that is installed upside down and aimed at a whiteboard wall. The camera does not support automatic rotation. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: In a SkypeSettings.xml file, set ContentCameraInverted to true.
Assign a Microsoft Teams Rooms Basic license.
From the Peripherals settings for Teams Rooms, clear Content enhancements.
Assign a Microsoft Teams Rooms Pro license.
In a SkypeSettings.xml file, set ContentCameraInverted to false.

A user named User1 reports that she cannot make calls because the Teams dial pad is not displayed.  
  
You run the `Get-CsOnlineUser` cmdlet and receive the output shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784111835544-z7it4r4t.png)

Assign a Microsoft Teams Phone Standard license to User1.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Routing user must be voice enabled and have a Direct Routing phone number. Assigning the number with `Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment` automatically enables Enterprise Voice. The existing MCOEV plan shows that the required Phone System capability is already assigned.

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You deploy a Teams device.  
  
You need to configure one-touch video calls so that they are routed to a predefined user.  
  
What should you implement?
questions.explanation:
A Hotline configures a Teams device to automatically call a predefined directory contact or phone number, providing the required direct one-touch route to the designated user. Microsoft documents Hotline/PLAR for Teams common-area phones as an autodial configuration for a preconfigured contact or PSTN number.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up common area phones for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/set-up-common-area-phones)

questions.question:
You have a Teams Phone deployment that includes a branch office.  
  
You need to restrict toll bypass for a user according to the office where the user is working during an inbound or outbound PSTN call.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Location-Based Routing restricts PSTN toll bypass according to the user's geographic/network location at the time of an inbound or outbound PSTN call. It uses the configured network topology, including network sites and IP subnets, to identify the office location.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan Location-Based Routing for Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/location-based-routing-plan)

questions.question:
You have a Teams Phone deployment that uses Direct Routing and a legacy PBX.  
  
You need to use the PBX for outbound calls from a scheduled Teams meeting.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
Teams meeting dial-out calls are Audio Conferencing calls. Routing them through Direct Routing to on-network destinations requires an Audio Conferencing routing policy (`OnlineAudioConferencingRoutingPolicy`), together with appropriate PBX routing configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [On-network Conferencing for Audio Conferencing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/audio-conferencing-on-network)

questions.question:
You are assessing the implementation of the technical requirements for the sales team.  
  
After the Watermark requirements have been implemented, which meeting feature will the sales team be able to use during Teams meetings?
questions.explanation:
Teams meeting watermarks for shared content are supported in PowerPoint Live, allowing participants to present PowerPoint content while the watermark protection is applied.\
\
**Learn more:** [Require a watermark for sensitive Teams meetings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/watermark-meeting-content-video)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You are deploying Direct Routing.  
  
All users have a SIP URI in the format `[email protected]`. The Session Border Controller (SBC) is named `sbc.voice.contoso.com`.  
  
While troubleshooting errors on the SBC, you receive the warning shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784115212772-cr1o2hno.png)  
  
What could be causing the issue?

options.text: Media bypass is disabled on the SBC
The firewall blocks inbound traffic on port 443 to the SBC
The firewall blocks traffic to the signaling port on the SBC
The firewall blocks outbound traffic on port 443 to Microsoft Teams

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams Direct Routing relies on SIP OPTIONS exchanges between the Microsoft SIP proxy and the SBC. The SBC’s configured SIP signaling port is its TLS listening port for Direct Routing; firewall rules that block traffic to that port prevent the OPTIONS exchange from succeeding.

**Learn more:** [Connect your Session Border Controller (SBC) to Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-connect-the-sbc) · [Direct Routing - SIP protocol](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-protocols-sip)

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You need to implement PSTN connectivity by using Direct Routing.  
  
Which three requirements are needed for the implementation? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a public DNS entry that maps the FQDN of the Session Border Controller (SBC) to a public IP address
a Session Border Controller (SBC) that uses a hostname in the onmicrosoft.com domain
a firewall rule that opens a TCP signaling port to Microsoft Teams
a firewall rule that opens a UDP signaling port to Microsoft Teams

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams Direct Routing requires a supported (certified) Session Border Controller (SBC), a public DNS record that maps the SBC FQDN to its public IP address, and firewall connectivity for SIP/TLS signaling over TCP. The SBC FQDN must use a registered tenant domain other than `*.onmicrosoft.com`; UDP applies to media transport, not SIP signaling. [Plan Direct Routing — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/microsoftteams/direct-routing-plan)

**Learn more:** [Plan Direct Routing — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/microsoftteams/direct-routing-plan) · [Session Border Controllers certified for Direct Routing — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-border-controllers)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You are deploying Direct Routing by using a certified Session Border Controller (SBC). The SBC FQDN is `sbc1.contoso.com`. You use signaling port `5067`.  
  
You are unable to place calls and receive an error message in the Microsoft Teams admin center, as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784128677657-5yf5ta6x.png)  
  
What could be causing the issue?

options.text: The failover timer is set to 0 seconds.
Calling plan licenses are not assigned to users.
The Forward P-Asserted Identify (PAI) header is disabled.
The Digicert root certificate is missing on the SBC.

questions.explanation:
Direct Routing uses mutual TLS between the SBC and Microsoft SIP infrastructure. If the required DigiCert root certificate is absent from the SBC trust store, the SBC cannot validate the SIP proxy certificate, so the TLS connection remains inactive and SIP signaling cannot support calls.

**Learn more:** [SBC connectivity issues - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/phone-system/direct-routing/sip-options-tls-certificate-issues) · [Connect your Session Border Controller (SBC) to Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-connect-the-sbc)

What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has offices in Paris and London.  
  
You are migrating from an on-premises PBX telephony solution to a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment that uses Direct Routing. You intend to retain the existing telephony carrier. The new solution will deliver telephony services to users in both offices.  
  
You need to recommend the solution that is most resilient to potential failures. The solution must ensure calls are routed through each user’s respective office.  
  
Which two actions should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure voice routing policies for each office.
Configure a single voice routing policy for all users.
Deploy a highly available Session Border Controller (SBC) pair to each office.
Deploy one Session Border Controller (SBC) to each office. Configure the SBCs as a high-availability pair.

questions.explanation:
Direct Routing call routing is based on a voice routing policy assigned to users, whose PSTN usages and voice routes identify the SBCs used for PSTN calls. Separate office-specific policies can direct Paris and London users to their respective local SBC routes. Each office also needs its own highly available SBC pair so that a local SBC failure does not remove that office’s telephony path.

You plan to implement toll bypass for the users in Canada. The solution must meet these requirements:

You are deploying Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
You must give a user a desk device that they can use while their computer is turned off. The device must meet these requirements:  
  
- Support calls.  
- Support video.  
- Support speed dial.  
- Display chat history.  
  
Which type of device should you provide?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams displays are all-in-one dedicated Teams devices for an individual user. They provide core Teams features including chat and calls, and they also support Teams phone capabilities such as speed dial and video-enabled calls. This satisfies the need for a standalone desk device that exposes chat history without relying on the user’s computer.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Teams displays](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/teams-displays) · [Phones for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/phones-for-teams)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has deployed Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
The company has a direct inward dial (DID) phone-number range from +14035554300 through +14035554329.  
  
Phone numbers +14035554310 through +14035554325 are assigned to Teams users, auto attendants, and call queues.  
  
You must ensure that, when an unassigned number is dialed, the caller is forwarded to a call queue named Reception.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Set Routing options to Person in organization and assign the Reception call queue.
Set Routing options to Voice application and assign the Reception call queue.
Add the DID range of +14035554300 to +14035554309 to the phone number range.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Phone numbers, select Routing rules, and then select Add a new rule.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Phone numbers, select Numbers, and then select Add.
Add the DID range of +14035554300 to +14035554329 to the phone number range.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams routes unassigned numbers through a routing rule created from **Voice > Phone numbers > Routing rules**. A call queue is selected as a **Voice application** destination. The full DID range can be used in the rule because numbers already assigned to users or resource accounts continue to route to their assigned targets, while unassigned numbers in that range are routed to Reception.

**Learn more:** [Configure routing options for unassigned phone numbers - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/routing-calls-to-unassigned-numbers)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You schedule a webinar named Meeting1.  
  
You need to ensure that users registering for Meeting1 must provide their organization name and job title.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Organization and Job title are predefined standard fields on a Teams webinar registration form. The webinar organizer configures the event’s registration form in the Teams client and can mark those fields as required. Tenant event policies only determine whether organizers are permitted to require standard registration questions.\
\

questions.explanation:
The **Busy on busy when in a call** setting determines how incoming calls are handled when a user is already in a call or conference. Setting it to **Unanswered** applies the user’s unanswered-call settings, such as routing the call to voicemail, rather than presenting the incoming call during the meeting.\

questions.explanation:
Teams Calling Policy busy options control incoming calls when a user is already in a call or conference. The **Use unanswered settings** option routes those calls according to the user’s unanswered-call settings, including voicemail, so calls received while the user is in a Teams meeting can be sent to voicemail. You create a new calling policy.  
  
What should you do next?
questions.explanation:
Teams IP phone policies enable hot desking on Teams phone/display endpoints, allowing users to temporarily sign in and access their personal Teams experience. Teams calling policies control the calling capabilities available on common-area and shared devices, including restricting ordinary private calling while emergency calling is handled through the configured PSTN service.

**Learn more:** [Set-CsTeamsIPPhonePolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsipphonepolicy?view=teams-ps) · [Set up common area phones for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/set-up-common-area-phones)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for the lunchroom device at the Toronto office.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Teams calling policies control whether common-area/shared devices can use call forwarding and simultaneous ring. A calling policy can therefore enable calls to the existing reception number to ring at both the reception area and the lunchroom device.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up common area phones for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/set-up-common-area-phones) · [Calling policies in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-calling-policy)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for the lunchroom device at the Toronto office.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Intelligent Speaker pilot depends on the Teams Rooms conferencing audio path: the conferencing microphone supplies the meeting audio used for transcription and speaker attribution, and the conferencing speaker provides meeting-call audio. The Default Speaker setting applies to audio from an HDMI ingest source, not conferencing audio. Microsoft documents that Intelligent Speaker enables in-room speaker identification in meeting transcripts and that Teams Rooms separately configures the microphone and speaker used for conferences.

**Learn more:** [Manage voice recognition for Intelligent Speaker](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/voice-recognition) · [Managing Teams Rooms on Windows settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/pro-portal-settings)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed Microsoft Teams Phone and have a call queue named Customer Service.  
  
You need to ensure that, when Customer Service agents place calls, the outbound calling name displays as Contoso and the caller ID displays the Customer Service phone number. Other users must **not** be affected.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, configure a new caller ID policy.
Set Calling Party Name to the organization name.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the global (Org-wide default) caller ID policy.
Set Replace the caller ID with to Resource account.
Set Override the caller ID policy to On.

questions.explanation:
A custom Teams caller ID policy can be assigned only to the Customer Service agents. Setting the Calling Party Name to Contoso supplies the outbound CNAM, and selecting Resource account as the caller ID replacement uses the phone number assigned to the call queue’s resource account. The global policy would affect users outside that group, and allowing caller-ID override would permit users to change the configured presentation.

**Learn more:** [Manage caller ID for users - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/caller-id-policies)

An eCDN optimizes delivery of a live-event video stream within an enterprise location, reducing the internet bandwidth consumed when many attendees watch simultaneously. Microsoft eCDN uses peer-to-peer distribution to offload the WAN connection, which directly addresses link saturation at a remote office.

You need to permit traffic from Microsoft 365 to a Session Border Controller (SBC).  
  
Which IP address ranges should be allowed through the firewall?
questions.explanation:

questions.question:

You configure Quality of Service (QoS) to prioritize network traffic for Teams communications.  
  
You need to validate the QoS configuration.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard, review Reliability Reports.
Perform a packet capture and validate the source port numbers.
From Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard, review Quality of Experience Reports.
Perform a packet capture and validate that the packets have DSCP markings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams QoS relies on DSCP markings to classify and prioritize real-time media traffic. Validation requires analyzing captured Teams traffic to confirm that DSCP values are present and have not been changed or stripped as traffic traverses the network.\
\

What should you do first?

options.text: Create a new enhanced encryption policy and enable end-to-end encryption for meetings.
Modify the global meeting policy and configure sensitive content detection.
Create a new meeting template and enable end-to-end encryption.
Create a new policy package and add a meeting policy and a messaging policy.

questions.explanation:
An enhanced encryption policy controls whether meeting organizers can use end-to-end meeting encryption. A meeting template can enforce end-to-end encryption only after that capability is enabled for the organizer, so the encryption policy is the prerequisite configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Require end-to-end encryption for sensitive Teams meetings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/MicrosoftTeams/end-to-end-encrypted-meetings)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for User2.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: For User2, unassign the Shared Calling policy.
From the Teams client of User2, configure Secondary Ringer.
Assign a new phone number to User2 as a private line.
Create a configuration profile, enable the hotline feature, and add a new phone number. Assign the profile to the Teams Phone device of User2.

questions.explanation:
A private line is a second, inbound-only phone number for a Teams user. Calls to a private line ignore inbound call-handling rules, including forwarding, simultaneous ringing, call groups, and delegation; therefore, a call to User2’s private number does not notify User3 as User2’s delegate.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure private lines in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/private-line)

options.text: Pin the Queues app for User1.

Add User1 as a call answering agent of the call queue.

questions.explanation:

Authorized users can make delegated call-queue configuration changes without being assigned a Teams administrative role.

options.text: The tenant is missing a vanity domain ofvoice.contoso.com.
The firewall blocks inbound traffic on port 443 to the SBC.
Microsoft 365 Phone System licenses are not assigned to the users.
The certificate does not match the FQDN of the SBC.

questions.explanation:
Direct Routing establishes TLS before exchanging SIP OPTIONS. The certificate presented by the SBC must have a Common Name or Subject Alternative Name that matches the SBC FQDN, `sbc.voice.contoso.com`. If it does not, the TLS connection is rejected and the SBC does not receive SIP OPTIONS from Microsoft.

**Learn more:** [SBC connectivity issues - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/phone-system/direct-routing/sip-options-tls-certificate-issues) · [Connect your Session Border Controller (SBC) to Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-connect-the-sbc)

You find that a newly deployed Teams Rooms device does not appear in the inventory.  
  
You need to discover that device.  
  
What should you do?

From the Resource Accounts settings, select Add account.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy a Microsoft Teams Rooms device named Device1 that will use a resource account named Resource1.  
  
You need to ensure that Resource1 is not prompted for multifactor authentication (MFA).  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure a Conditional Access policy that excludes Resource1.
From Teams settings, set Require a secondary form of authentication to access meeting content to No access.
Configure a Conditional Access policy that includes Device1.
Configure a Conditional Access policy that includes Resource1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams Rooms resource accounts should not use user-interactive MFA, because a room device cannot complete an MFA approval request. Excluding the resource account from the Conditional Access policy that requires MFA prevents that policy from prompting the account while allowing separate, supported controls to secure the device.

Which two device types satisfy these requirements? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams Rooms supports dual front-of-room displays on both Windows and Android. Teams displays and Teams audio conference phones are not Teams Rooms systems designed to support two front-of-room displays.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.

Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each selected choice is worth one point.

options.text: Configure call flow for business hours and after hours.

questions.explanation:

**Learn more:** [Manage resource accounts for Teams Phone Agent, Auto attendants and Call Queue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-manage-resource-accounts) · [Setup Auto Attendant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-auto-attendant)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a PBX phone system containing 100 handsets. The handsets support SIP registration.  
  
You deploy a new Microsoft Teams Phone environment with SIP Gateway configured.  
  
You need to register the handsets with Teams.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, create a configuration profile for each device. Configure the handsets to use LLDP.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, create a configuration profile for each device. Add the Teams SIP device details to the handsets.
From the voice calling policy, set SIP devices can be used for calls to On. Configure the provisioning URL on the handsets.
From the voice calling policy, set SIP devices can be used for calls to On. Configure the handsets to use LLDP.

questions.explanation:
Teams SIP Gateway users must be assigned a calling policy in which **SIP devices can be used for calls** is enabled. The SIP phones must also be pointed to the SIP Gateway provisioning server URL, configured manually on the handset or centrally through DHCP. LLDP is relevant to certain dynamic emergency-location scenarios, not SIP Gateway registration.

**Learn more:** [Configure SIP Gateway - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/sip-gateway-configure)

questions.question:

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:

You need to enable PSTN services for 100 new users while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
Which cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
`Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment` assigns a PSTN phone number to a user and supports `CallingPlan`, `DirectRouting`, and `OperatorConnect` phone-number types. Assigning the number automatically sets the user’s Enterprise Voice status to enabled, making it the appropriate cmdlet for provisioning PSTN calling users.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying Direct Routing by using a certified Session Border Controller (SBC). The SBC FQDN is `sbc1.contoso.com`. You use signaling port 5067.  
  
You cannot make calls and receive an error message in the Microsoft Teams admin center, as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784123840803-hf2r68y5.png)  
  
What could be causing the issue?

options.text: The firewall blocks traffic on port 5067.
Licenses are not assigned to the contoso.com domain.
Location-Based Routing is enabled for the SBC.

questions.explanation:
The SBC’s configured SIP signaling port is the TLS listening port used for Direct Routing communication. If a firewall blocks traffic on port 5067, Microsoft Teams cannot establish or maintain TLS connectivity to the SBC, so the SBC is shown as inactive and calls cannot be placed.

**Learn more:** [Connect your Session Border Controller (SBC) to Direct Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-connect-the-sbc) · [SBC connectivity issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/phone-system/direct-routing/sip-options-tls-certificate-issues)

What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice, select Dial plan, and then select Add.

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment with Teams devices in meeting rooms and public areas. You need to enable Device lock on the devices.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
For shared Teams phones in public areas and meeting rooms, an administrator configures the device lock/PIN setting through a Teams device configuration profile. Configuration profiles manage device-specific settings and can be assigned to the relevant devices.\
\

What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
`QRCodeAutoAcceptProximateMeetingInvitations` controls automatic acceptance of proximity-based meeting invitations initiated through a QR code. Setting it to `false` disables automatic acceptance, so the room console must be used to manually accept the meeting invitation.

**Learn more:** [Join meetings on Teams Rooms using a QR code](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/teams-rooms-qr-codes) · [Manage a Microsoft Teams Rooms console settings remotely with an XML configuration file](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/xml-config-file)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a main office in Seattle and a branch office in Portland.  
  
The company has a Microsoft 365 E3 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You configure and assign a network roaming policy to each office.  
  
You need to ensure that, when a user joins a meeting from either office, the assigned network roaming policy settings are applied.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: From Meeting settings, enable Quality of Service (QoS) markers
From Meeting policies, set Network configuration lookup to On
From Meeting policies, set Local broadcasting to On
From Network topology, set Location based routing to On
From Network topology, add a network site

questions.explanation:
Teams network roaming policies are assigned to network sites and are selected dynamically according to the site from which the Teams client connects. For users who are not Enterprise Voice enabled, Teams requires the meeting-policy setting `AllowNetworkConfigurationSettingsLookup` to be enabled; in the Teams admin center, this is **Network configuration lookup** set to **On**.

**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [Teams settings and policies reference - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/settings-policies-reference)

You have a Microsoft Teams deployment that includes a Teams Rooms on Windows device named Device1.  
  
You need to make sure that Device1 can join third-party meetings.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On Device1, update the SkypeSettings.xml file.
Assign a Teams Rooms Pro license to Device1.
To Device1, import the X.509 certificate for the third-party meeting provider.

questions.explanation:
Teams Rooms on Windows can enable third-party meeting providers by setting the appropriate values in `SkypeSettings.xml`, such as `WebexMeetingsEnabled`, `ZoomMeetingsEnabled`, or `GoogleMeetMeetingsEnabled` to `True`. Teams Admin Center configuration profiles for this capability apply to Teams Rooms on Android, not Windows.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Teams Phone deployment with two sites, named Site1 and Site2. Each site has a Session Border Controller (SBC).  
  
You have a user named User1.  
  
User1 moves from Site1 to Site2 and receives a new phone number.  
  
You need to modify a policy assigned to User1 so that the SBC at Site2 is used when the user places outbound calls.  
  
What should you change?
questions.explanation:
A voice routing policy is assigned to a Teams user and contains PSTN usages that map to voice routes. Each voice route specifies the online PSTN gateway, which is the pointer to an SBC. Assigning User1 a voice routing policy that uses the Site2 route causes outbound calls to use the Site2 SBC.

**Learn more:** [Configure call routing for Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-voice-routing) · [Manage call routing policies for Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-voice-routing-policies)

Your network has an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named contoso.com.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You plan to implement shared-room video conferencing by using Microsoft Teams Rooms.  
  
You deploy 50 Teams Rooms on Windows devices and join every device to contoso.com.  
  
You need to enable Direct Guest Join on all 50 devices. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select all the devices, and then add a tag.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, configure a configuration policy.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, select all the devices, and then modify the Meeting settings.

questions.explanation:
Direct Guest Join is enabled through Teams Rooms device meeting settings. Applying the meeting-setting change to all selected Teams Rooms on Windows devices enables the capability in bulk, minimizing per-device administration. Device tags are organizational only, configuration profiles target Teams Rooms on Android, and `Set-CsTeamsGuestMeetingConfiguration` configures meeting features for Teams guest users rather than Teams Rooms Direct Guest Join.

**Learn more:** [Third-party meetings on Teams Rooms](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/third-party-join) · [Set-CsTeamsGuestMeetingConfiguration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsguestmeetingconfiguration?view=teams-ps)

You need to enable Microsoft Teams users to make PSTN calls through a Session Border Controller (SBC).  
  
Which licenses can you assign to meet this goal?
questions.explanation:
Teams Direct Routing connects a customer-provided SBC to Teams Phone for PSTN calling. Direct Routing users require Microsoft Teams and Teams Phone. Microsoft 365 E5 and Office 365 E5 are the listed E5 suites that support Teams Phone with a separate PSTN connectivity option such as Direct Routing; E3 requires an additional Teams Phone license.\

questions.question:
You are assessing the implementation of the technical requirements for the sales team.  
  
After those requirements are implemented, which meeting feature will the sales team be able to use during Teams meetings?
questions.explanation:
Teams meeting watermarks for shared content are supported with PowerPoint Live. This lets protected shared presentation content display the participant-specific watermark required for the sales team.\
\
**Learn more:** [Require a watermark for sensitive Teams meetings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/watermark-meeting-content-video)

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You deploy a new network site.  
  
You find that the new site does not appear in location-based reports, although other sites do appear.  
  
You need to ensure that every site appears in the reports.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard select Tenant Data Upload and upload a CSV file that contains all the network sites.
From Network planner in the Microsoft Teams admin center, add a new persona.
From Network planner in the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify an existing network plan.
From Network planner in the Microsoft Teams admin center, add a new network plan.
From the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard, select Tenant Data Upload and upload a CSV file that contains the new network site only.

questions.explanation:
Call Quality Dashboard location-enhanced reporting uses uploaded tenant/building data to associate network IP ranges and subnets with physical locations. Updating and uploading the complete CSV, including the new site, maintains the mappings for existing sites and adds the new site's mapping. Microsoft Learn also directs administrators to modify the original building file by adding new subnets and re-upload it when mappings are missing.

**Learn more:** [Building and endpoint data - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/cqd-upload-tenant-building-data) · [Data and reports in Call Quality Dashboard (CQD) - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/cqd-data-and-reports)

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment and implement Teams Rooms on Windows.  
  
You need to apply a custom theme to the Team1 Teams Rooms on Windows display.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Teams Rooms on Windows applies custom display themes through the `<Theming>` configuration in a `SkypeSettings.xml` file. This file supports theme names and custom background settings for the room display.\

You have a Microsoft Teams Phone deployment and implement Teams Rooms on Windows.  
  
You need to apply a custom theme to the Team1 Teams Rooms on Windows display.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Teams live events policies control whether assigned users can schedule live events. Disabling Live events scheduling in the org-wide live events policy prevents all users from creating them; live event settings only configure organization-wide event options, not scheduling permission.

**Learn more:** [Teams settings and policies reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/settings-policies-reference) · [Set up for live events in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-live-events/set-up-for-teams-live-events)

What should you do?

options.text: In the SkypeSettings.xml file, set EnablePublicPreview to true.
Add Device1 to the Staging ring.

You have a Microsoft Teams deployment that includes a Teams Rooms on Windows device named Device1.  
  
You need to manually update the Teams app on Device1 to the latest version.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Run the Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment cmdlet and specify the -PhoneNumber parameter.
Assign a Microsoft Teams Phone Standard license to User1.
Run the New-CsHybridTelephoneNumber and specify the -TelephoneNumber parameter.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Routing user must have a Teams Phone license and a Direct Routing phone number assigned. Assigning the phone number by using `Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment` sets `EnterpriseVoiceEnabled` to `True` automatically. User1 currently has no line URI and has `EnterpriseVoiceEnabled` set to `False`; the existing `HybridVoice` policy indicates that a voice routing policy is already assigned.

**Learn more:** [Enable users for Direct Routing - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/direct-routing-enable-users) · [Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csphonenumberassignment?view=teams-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed Microsoft Teams Phone. The `613 7010 5XXX` phone-number range is assigned to the Session Border Controller (SBC).  
  
A user named User1 is configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784114905456-9nc4mrio.png)  
  
User1 reports that, when an external caller tries to call User1's phone number, the external caller receives an error message.  
  
User1 can place outbound calls, but no caller ID is displayed.  
  
Which two commands should you run to resolve the issues? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A phone number that is routed through an SBC must be assigned as a Direct Routing number. Removing its Calling Plan assignment and reassigning the same number with the DirectRouting type corrects the number assignment for SBC-based inbound routing and lets the number be used as the outbound calling identity. Assigning a phone number automatically enables Enterprise Voice, so no separate EnterpriseVoiceEnabled change is required.

**Learn more:** [Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csphonenumberassignment?view=teams-ps) · [Remove-CsPhoneNumberAssignment (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/remove-csphonenumberassignment?view=teams-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a network region called Region1 in Microsoft Teams.  
  
You are adding a network site to Region1. The site has a 1.5-Mb connection.  
  
You need to ensure that every user at the site has a good voice experience.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Tag all traffic with a DSCP value of 46.
Assign the Region1 users a meeting policy that has IP video disabled.
Create and assign a Teams Network Roaming Policy that has IP video disabled.
Assign the Region1 users a meeting policy that has a media bit rate of 1,500 Kbs.

questions.explanation:
A Teams Network Roaming Policy is assigned to a network site and is applied dynamically when a Teams client connects from that site. Disabling IP video at the low-bandwidth site reduces media-bandwidth demand so that voice traffic can retain the available capacity. The policy is specifically intended for location-based video and media bitrate controls.

**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [New-CsTeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsnetworkroamingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing a user named User1. The subscription uses Microsoft Teams Phone, and User1 has a Teams Phone Standard license.  
  
You find that User1 cannot route calls from external phone numbers to voicemail.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can route calls to voicemail.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign User1 a Teams Premium license.
Modify the voice routing policies assigned to User1.
Modify the calling policy assigned to User1.
Modify the external access policy assigned to User1.

questions.explanation:
A Teams Calling Policy controls whether inbound calls can be routed to Cloud Voicemail. Configure User1’s assigned calling policy so that **Voicemail for inbound calls** is set to **On** or **Let users decide**.

**Learn more:** [Set up Cloud Voicemail - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-phone-system-voicemail) · [Calling policies in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-calling-policy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You are planning a meeting space that includes a Teams-certified conference phone. You need to configure the phone to meet these requirements:  
  
- Display the calendar by default.  
- Support one-touch join for Teams meetings.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create and assign a Teams IP phone policy
Assign a Microsoft Teams Rooms Pro license to the phone
Assign a Shared Device license to the phone
Create and assign an Audio Conferencing policy
Enable the Cloud Video Interop for Teams service

questions.explanation:
A Teams Rooms Pro license is required for a small meeting room’s audio-conferencing device to join meetings with one touch. Assigning a Teams IP Phone policy with `MeetingSignIn` enables the meeting interface, which provides the Calendar app and meeting-join experience. A Shared Device license supplies common-area calling functionality but does not provide calendar support.

**Learn more:** [Plan your deployment for Teams Phones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/plan-device-deployment) · [Set Microsoft Teams Phone device user interface](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/teams-android-devices-user-interface)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Teams deployment.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a network region called Region1 in Microsoft Teams.  
  
You are adding a network site to Region1. The site has a 1.5-Mb connection.  
  
You need to ensure that every user at the site has a good voice experience.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign the Region1 users a meeting policy that has Broadcast production with NDI and SDI hardware disabled.
Assign the Region1 users a meeting policy that has a media bit rate of 1,500 Kbs.
Create and assign a Teams Network Roaming Policy that has Video Conferencing disabled.
Set Insert Quality of Service (QoS) markers for real-time media traffic to On.

questions.explanation:
A Teams Network Roaming Policy can be assigned to a network site and dynamically applies media controls to clients connected there. Disabling IP video on a constrained 1.5-Mb connection preserves available bandwidth for voice traffic, helping maintain voice quality for all users at that site. The policy’s media controls include IP video and media bit rate, and it is applied to network sites rather than directly to users.

**Learn more:** [Manage video and media settings with the network roaming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [New-CsTeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsnetworkroamingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

questions.question:
Solution: Run `New-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy` and set the `-MediaBitRateKb` parameter to `1`.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`MediaBitRateKb` limits the aggregate media bit rate for audio, video, and video-based app sharing; it does not prohibit users from enabling video. Site-specific control requires a Teams network roaming policy assigned to the network site, with `AllowIPVideo` set to `false`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [New-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

questions.domain: Plan and design collaboration communications systems
questions.question:
Solution: Run `New-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy` and set the `-AllowIPVideo` parameter to `$False`.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Teams meeting policy is not applied dynamically by corporate network site. Location-specific video control requires a `TeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy` with `AllowIPVideo` set to `$false`, assigned to the relevant network site; Teams then applies that setting when a client connects from that site.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage video and media settings with the network roaming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [New-CsTeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsnetworkroamingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

questions.domain: Configure and manage Teams meetings, webinars, and town halls
questions.question:
Solution: You execute `New-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy` and configure the `-IPVideoMode` parameter as `DISABLED`.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`New-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy` only creates a meeting policy; it does not assign that policy to the affected users or scope it to a particular corporate site. Setting `IPVideoMode` to `DISABLED` prohibits incoming and outgoing video only for users to whom that meeting policy applies.\
\
**Learn more:** [New-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps) · [Meeting policy settings for audio & video](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video)

questions.domain: Configure and manage Teams meetings, webinars, and town halls
questions.question:
Solution: Run `New-CsTeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy` and set the `-AllowIPVideo` parameter to `$False`.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Setting `AllowIPVideo` to `$False` in a Teams Network Roaming Policy prohibits video in meetings and calls, but creating the policy alone does not apply it at any corporate site. The policy must be assigned to the applicable network site by using `Set-CsTenantNetworkSite -NetworkRoamingPolicy`; without that assignment, it cannot enforce the site-specific restriction.\
\
**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [New-CsTeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsnetworkroamingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You have a Microsoft Teams deployment.  
  
You are deploying a domain-joined Teams Rooms on Windows device.  
  
You find that the device cannot proceed beyond the Windows sign-in screen.  
  
You need to ensure that the device can perform automatic sign-in.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams Pro Rooms Management portal, enroll the device.

questions.explanation:
Teams Rooms on Windows requires the Windows AutoAdminLogon setting to remain enabled for the device to boot into the Teams Rooms experience. In a domain-joined deployment, Group Policy can override this and other required settings. Teams Rooms devices should have Group Policy exclusions, typically through a separate OU with inheritance blocked, so policies that prevent automatic sign-in are not applied.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named contoso.com.
